title: Singapore Armed Forces Recruitment 2026 Guide
metaDescription: Singapore Armed Forces recruitment 2026: National Service rules, enlistment age, two-year service, IPPT reduction, medical grading and regular careers.
headline: Singapore Armed Forces Recruitment 2026: NS and Careers

sections.title: National Service: Who Must Serve
sections.content:
National Service is mandatory in Singapore under the Enlistment Act 1970. All male Singapore citizens and second-generation male permanent residents must serve, usually in the Singapore Armed Forces, the Singapore Police Force or the Singapore Civil Defence Force. First-generation permanent residents who gained PR status as adults are generally exempt, although their sons are not.

The process starts early. From the age of 13, liable males receive NS notices by post, and at 16 years and six months they must register for National Service through the OneNS portal run by the Central Manpower Base. Most enlist at around 18, after a medical screening that decides their fitness and vocation.

sections.title: From Registration to Enlistment Day
sections.content:
After registration, every pre-enlistee attends a medical screening at the Central Manpower Base. Until the October 2027 intake, fitness is graded under the Physical Employment Standard, known as PES, which shapes the vocation and training a recruit receives. From October 2027, PES is replaced by a refreshed medical classification system with clearer information on fitness, exemptions and eligibility for a shorter service.

Those who want to start early can apply for the Voluntary Early Enlistment Scheme from the age of 16.5, with a parent or guardian consent. Successful applicants join the next available intake, but they cannot disrupt their service later to pursue pre-university studies. Everyone else receives an enlistment notice telling them where and when to report.

sections.title: How Long You Serve and What Shortens It
sections.content:
Full-time National Service lasts two years for most enlistees. Combat-fit pre-enlistees who pass the Individual Physical Proficiency Test before enlisting, scoring at least 61 points, serve eight weeks less, bringing their service down to one year and ten months. Basic Military Training lasts between nine and seventeen weeks depending on medical grade and vocation.

Service does not end at ORD, the operationally ready date. After full-time service, national servicemen become operationally ready reservists and attend in-camp training of about five to seven days a year, normally until age 40, or age 50 for officers. Ignoring NS notices is an offence under the Enlistment Act, punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 dollars, jail of up to three years, or both.

sections.title: Pay, Regular Careers and How to Apply
sections.content:
Full-time national servicemen receive a monthly allowance that rises with rank and time in service. At recruit level it started from about 630 Singapore dollars a month in recent years, with higher allowances for specialists and officers. Regular careers in the SAF are separate from National Service and are open to Singapore citizens through MINDEF and SAF career channels.

Regulars sign on as officers, warrant officers, specialists or military experts, with structured training, promotion paths and benefits. Applications go through the official MINDEF careers portal, where candidates choose a service and vocation, then attend interviews, medical checks and fitness tests before enlistment.

faqs.q: Who must serve National Service in Singapore?
faqs.a: All male Singapore citizens and second-generation male permanent residents must serve National Service, normally in the Singapore Armed Forces, police or civil defence force. They register at 16.5 years old and usually enlist at around 18. First-generation permanent residents who obtained PR status as adults are generally exempt, but their sons must still serve.

faqs.q: How long is full-time National Service in Singapore?
faqs.a: Full-time National Service lasts two years for most enlistees. Combat-fit pre-enlistees who score at least 61 points in the pre-enlistee Individual Physical Proficiency Test serve eight weeks less, completing one year and ten months instead. Basic Military Training takes nine to seventeen weeks, depending on medical grade and vocation.

faqs.q: Can I enlist for National Service before turning 18?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Voluntary Early Enlistment Scheme, you can enlist from the age of 16.5 with the consent of a parent or guardian. You apply online and email the signed form to the Central Manpower Base, and successful applicants join the next available intake. However, early enlistees cannot disrupt service later for pre-university studies.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore my National Service notices?
faqs.a: Ignoring National Service notices is an offence under the Enlistment Act 1970. Offenders can be fined up to 10,000 dollars, jailed for up to three years, or both. The obligation does not disappear: you must still complete the service. Anyone with genuine difficulties should contact the Central Manpower Base early to discuss deferment or other options.
